about: Pairs of passages from two different sites that both state the same claim (item 030). Each pair is labelled 'retold' or 'independent'.

Labels were written before any code or threshold existed. The passages were written by the assistant, modelled on common patterns (rewritten articles, restated rumours, outlets reporting the same event with their own details); they are not taken from real pages.

Label rule: 'independent' when each passage has at least one specific the other lacks (a name, figure, date, place, quote, ground or detail). 'retold' when one of them adds nothing the other lacks, so it could have been written from the other, including two bare statements of the claim.

A retelling that adds its own invented detail is labelled 'independent' by this rule: telling it from an independent report needs knowing where each page got its information, which the text does not show.

How the threshold is chosen, fixed before measuring: on the dev set only. If the two labels separate, the midpoint between the lowest 'retold' and the highest 'independent' similarity; otherwise the threshold with the highest accuracy on dev, ties broken towards fewer independent pairs folded. The held-out set is then run once with that threshold.
